new_statements.quote: Other languages where these patterns have been reported include at least Pangasinan, Balangaw, Isnag, Ibanag, Central Cagayan Agta, Ifugao (see Blust and Trussel ongoing; Healey 1960; Reid 1971), Northern Subanan (Daguman 2013: 47), Sarangani Manobo (DuBois 1976) Sangil (Sneddon 1984: 24) and Tiruray (Schlegel 1971: 7). All Philippine language data discussed so far show stress-shift to the final syllable after a penultimate schwa. [Supporting survey, Blust 2013: 179:] In almost all languages of Mindanao stress is penultimate (Subanen, Manobo, Danaw languages), or final (Bilic languages).
new_statements.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2023. Reconstructing non-contrastive stress in Austronesian and the role of the mora in stress shift, gemination and vowel shift. Diachronica (online-first). doi:10.1075/dia.20032.smi -- citing Daguman, Josephine S. 2013. A grammar of Northern Subanen. Outstanding Grammars from Australia 13. Munich: LINCOM, p.47
new_statements.locator: section 3.2.1, pp. [12]-[13] (online-first pagination; PDF page 12), paragraph following example (4)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-hand only: primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable, non-contrastively, except that it shifts to the final syllable when the penult contains a schwa (Smith 2023 reporting Daguman 2013: 47). Blust 2013 independently groups Subanen with the Mindanao languages that have lost contrastive stress and are regularly penultimate.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source examined.
new_statements.exceptions: Schwa penult repels stress to the final syllable (per Smith 2023 citing Daguman 2013: 47). No further detail (loanwords, closed penults, clitics) available second-hand.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement as reported; Smith's context is the historical stress-shift pattern (*CəCVC roots), not a full synchronic description. Lobel 2013: 313-314 notes that Subanen phrases 'sound like single phonological words', so the word/phrase domain in Northern Subanen is unverified until Daguman 2013 ch. on phonology is read.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources concern Northern Subanen [stb] = nort2885 (Daguman's data from Katipunan/Dipolog/Polanco area, Zamboanga del Norte; Wikipedia/Ethnologue alt names Tuboy Subanon, Salug-Godod Subanen). Smith 2023 spells it 'Northern Subanan' but cites Daguman 2013 A grammar of Northern Subanen. Blust 2013's 'Subanen' is the group, not a specific variety. Sister-language first-hand statements exist on file for Central/Sindangan Subanen [syb] cent2089 (Brichoux 1977: no contrastive word stress) and must not be attributed to nort2885.
